# Decisions: scanner-version-gate

- 2026-08-06T13:30:48.908Z — chose **Version-gate the `@source not` repair on what the host will actually build with: read node_modules/tailwindcss's version when installed, else the declared range's LOWER bound, and write only when that is known >= 4.1. Below it (or when unknowable) doctor still FAILs the hazard but writes nothing, and names the 4.0-compatible remedy — narrowing the import scan base with `source(<dir>)` — computed relative to THAT stylesheet. cssExcludesSofar now also counts a narrowed `source(...)`/`source(none)` as protection.** over Emitting `@source not` unconditionally on tailwindcss>=4 (the shipped behaviour, which broke a 4.0.17 host's build); trusting the declared range optimistically so `^4` counts as 4.1; auto-rewriting the import to add `source(...)` on pre-4.1 hosts; downgrading the finding to WARN when no fix is available. because `@source not` landed in Tailwind 4.1 — verified by unpacking both tarballs (the `not ` prefix is parsed only in 4.1.0's dist, absent in 4.0.17) and reproduced live: on real 4.0.17 the inserted line fails the build with "Error: `@source` paths must be quoted", because `not` reads as an unquoted path. A defense that breaks the build it defends is worse than the hazard, so the fix must never be written on a version that cannot parse it, and an ambiguous range must resolve conservatively (`^4` guarantees only 4.0). Auto-adding `source(...)` was rejected because narrowing the scan base silently stops scanning templates outside it — a content-loss edit, not the safe deterministic repair --fix is scoped to (D-P10/BD54); it is offered as a hint the user applies.
